absent: Implementation and verdict logic of the checked runner, and numeric meanings of success versus failure expectations.
Numeric values and bit layout of lock type tags, and behavior of the realtime guard and continuation output.
Definitions of wound wait shorthand operations, object and context layouts, stamp ordering, and slow path entry conditions.
Interrupt entry and exit, lock and unlock shorthand, spin and read lock layouts, and reclaim and allocation flag semantics.
No exported interfaces, stable ABI constants, or persistent data layouts are observable in these fragments.

findings.text: A small reporting helper emits a test label right aligned in a fixed width field followed by a colon through the kernel log facility. Callers invoke it before running one or more checked cases so that follow on continuation output appears on the same line.

Single case helpers run one generated read write lock scenario whose name combines a base and numeric suffix. Plain variants record an expected pass or fail outcome while recursive variants first emit a column separator to align follow on output. All of them frame the run with the label helper and a line terminator.

Small group helpers exercise spin plus write and read acquisition under one label. The three case form expects failure for spin and write acquisition but success for read acquisition while a widened form also accepts a combined spin or read write type for the spin case. Two case forms cover write versus read only with hard and soft interrupt qualified duplicates guarded for non realtime builds.

Combinatorial helpers expand a single logical scenario over all orderings of three elements and over interrupt contexts. Six entry families run every permutation of the numeric suffixes while six lock families probe spin, write, read, mutex, semaphore and realtime mutex members together with a uniform expected outcome except a read tolerant family that expects success only for the read member.

The wound wait self test abstracts its underlying primitive through a build selected alias set. One alternative forwards blocking, try, nested, interruptible, killable and unlock operations to the realtime mutex family while the other forwards the same six operations to the normal mutex family. Test bodies use only the abstract names so the same scenarios run under either configuration.

The failure acquire scenario validates the wound wait return code contract. After context initialization and a stamp advance, first acquisition must establish context and succeed while immediate reacquire by the same context must report EALREADY and acquisition by a newer contender must report EDEADLK. The scenario then releases, rechecks try acquisition cleanup, and exercises a debug only warning path when allocation debugging is enabled.

Normal mutex entry points must not engage wound wait bookkeeping. The test seeds the object context field with a distinctive sentinel value, invokes each base operation including blocking, interruptible, killable, succeeding and failing try, and nested variants, then requires the sentinel to remain unchanged after unlock. This establishes isolation between plain mutex use and wound wait contexts.

A family of negative scenarios defines forbidden wound wait lifecycle transitions. Creating two active contexts, clearing the debug class field, completing or releasing a context twice, finalizing while a lock is held, acquiring after completion, unlocking an object twice, clearing the acquired count before unlock, and acquiring with a stale foreign context are all treated as failures that must trigger the checking harness.

Deadlock recovery scenarios establish an older stamp holder on a second and optionally third object using base locking with dependency tracking temporarily released, then require a younger contender to observe deadlock on the second object. Correct handling releases held objects, restores dependency tracking and base unlock, and retries through either the fast path or the slow path. Retrying without first releasing, acquiring additional objects after deadlock, or acquiring a different object after partial cleanup are treated as failures.

Spin nesting through a held base object is permitted while nesting through an unheld base is rejected. One positive scenario nests under separately held outer locks with balanced acquire and release while the negative scenario nests directly under an unlocked base and must fail.

The wound wait driver emits a banner and runs ordered sections with fixed pass or fail expectations under one lock type. Interface checks expect success for failure handling and normal use but failure for unneeded slow entry. Context mixing, double completion, double release, early finalization, post completion acquisition, double object unlock, unbalanced accounting and stale context checks all expect failure. Deadlock checks expect success only when the holder is released before retry through either fast or slow entry and failure otherwise, while spin nesting expects failure when unheld and success when held.

The same driver then presents a table of initiator versus follower interactions. A context initiator fails against a blocking follower but succeeds against try and context followers. A try initiator fails against blocking and context followers but succeeds against another try. A blocking initiator fails against blocking and context followers but succeeds against try. A spin initiator fails against blocking and context followers but succeeds against try.

Queued read lock interaction with hard interrupt context depends on acquisition order. Reading then locking inside the handler while locking then reading outside is rejected while the opposite order is accepted. A third inversion mixing an empty handler section with a disabled interrupt lock plus read section and a plain read section is rejected.

Filesystem reclaim nesting requires that code holding a kernel reclaim scope only perform allocations that cannot recurse into the filesystem. Allocating with a no filesystem scope inside a kernel scope is allowed while allocating with a kernel scope is rejected unless wrapped by a save that temporarily enforces no filesystem semantics and a matching restore before scope release.

Two small drivers emit banner headers and run their suites through the common checked runner. The queued read lock driver runs three hard interrupt orderings with failure, success and failure expectations under the read write lock type. The filesystem reclaim driver runs correct, wrong and protected nestings with success, failure and success expectations and no lock type.
